### Government, DoD, DOE, NASA, and Similar Organization Announcements

**Quantum Tech**
*   The U.S. government, under the CHIPS Act, is acquiring minority equity stakes in quantum computing companies D-Wave Quantum, Rigetti Computing, and Quantinuum, providing each with $100 million in research and development grants. This funding aims to scale quantum-computing research and strengthen domestic semiconductor and advanced-hardware supply chains. Rigetti Computing will use its funds to address bottlenecks in scaling superconducting quantum processors, expanding cryogenic capacity, and accelerating manufacturing. D-Wave Quantum plans to advance microelectronics R&D for advanced semiconductor prototyping and scalable high-performance quantum hardware. Quantinuum will focus on building scalable, reliable integrated photonics engines through partnerships with GlobalFoundries for ion trap fabrication and Monarch Quantum for integrated lasers and optical components.
*   GlobalFoundries also secured a separate $375 million agreement with the U.S. government to expand domestic quantum manufacturing capabilities, supporting the transition from lab prototypes to commercial-scale quantum processing units.
*   PsiQuantum finalized an agreement with the U.S. Department of Commerce for a $100 million grant under the CHIPS Act to support research and local production of key hardware components like optical switches and photon detectors. Additionally, PsiQuantum signed a $125 million contract with DARPA in July 2026 to test commercial pathways for quantum computing systems.
*   Northrop Grumman successfully flight-tested a quantum-enabled navigation system developed with SandboxAQ on its Lumberjack attack drone. This technology allows for navigation without GPS, crucial in jammed or GPS-denied environments.

**Drone Tech & Robotics**
*   DoD Solution and Estonian Defsecintel are jointly developing drone interception systems, combining Defsecintel's EIRSHIELD system for AI-based target detection with DoD Solution's AURA AI onboard autonomy platform.
*   The Pennsylvania National Guard's Unmanned Aircraft System Training and Innovation Facility demonstrated "Project R.E.D." (Recovery Exploitation Drone), which uses a drone with a robotic arm to recover downed adversary or friendly drones. This project won the innovation category at the U.S. Army's first Best Drone Warfighter Competition.
*   The U.S. Air Force is seeking "rapidly deployable" drone swarms for base security, aiming to transform cargo planes into "adaptive, force-multiplying launch platforms" to deploy drone swarms.
*   The Advanced Research Projects Agency for Health (ARPA-H), within the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services, awarded up to $17.5 million to Kitware and the University of North Carolina (UNC) for the Testbed for Autonomous Interventions and Robotics (TAIR) project. This funding will develop an open-source virtual testing platform for robotic stroke interventions, aiming to create an endovascular robot for catheter navigation to treat conditions like stroke and aneurysm.
*   The Department of Energy (DOE), Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), National Science Foundation (NSF), and National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) are collaborating to build autonomous laboratories leveraging robotics and edge AI to enable self-driving experimentation.
*   The Missile Defense Agency (MDA) offers STEM Boosting Engineering, Science, and Technology (BEST) Robotics Grants of up to $30,000 to local competition hubs for K-12 and college robotics programs.

**Space Tech & Satellite Communication**
*   Boeing secured a $2 billion contract from the U.S. Space Force for the Mobile User Objective System Service Life Extension (MUOS SLE) program. This contract involves two narrowband communications satellites, with the first delivery anticipated in 2031, to extend and improve secure military communications globally.
*   Space Systems Command (SSC) awarded Boeing a $2.8 billion contract to build and deliver the first two satellites for the Evolved Strategic Satellite Communications (ESS) program, which aims to modernize nuclear command, control, and communications capabilities.
*   NASA selected 41 commercial technology projects from 37 American companies as part of its 2025 Announcement of Collaboration Opportunity (ACO). These projects focus on developing capabilities for future Moon and Mars missions, including space transportation, planetary surface operations, and infrastructure for long-term lunar exploration.
*   NASA is actively seeking proposals to advance lunar surface technologies, including vertical solar array technology for power, in-situ resource utilization for oxygen extraction, radioisotope Stirling generators (nuclear energy for spacecraft), in-space advanced manufacturing, and innovative nanomaterials production.
*   NASA awarded Blue Origin a contract to develop the agency's Mars Telecommunications Network, a next-generation communications system.
*   All.space received a federal agreement to scale satellite communications using its Hydra technology, aiming to accelerate the production and qualification of resilient satellite communication terminals.
*   Iridium Communications Inc. was awarded a five-year indefinite delivery/indefinite quantity contract from the U.S. Space Force's Space Systems Command Commercial Space Office (COMSO) with a potential value of up to $85.8 million for EMSS infrastructure upgrades.
*   Sierra Space has secured $1.5 billion in national security and defense contracts since 2023, including a "Quick Start" Resilient GPS (R-GPS) contract from the U.S. Space Force for designing smaller, more cost-effective GPS satellites.

**Nuclear Energy**
*   The U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) finalized a loan of up to $1.9 billion to NextEra Energy to support the restart of the Duane Arnold Energy Center nuclear power plant in Iowa. This plant, expected to restart by early 2029, is primarily intended to provide power to Google's artificial intelligence data centers.
*   The DOE has made conditional commitments to provide high-assay low-enriched uranium (HALEU) to NASA and Radiant Industries, Inc. to meet near-term fuel needs.
*   The DOE announced conditional selections for Westinghouse and Radiant to conduct the first tests in the Demonstration of Microreactor Experiments (DOME) facility at Idaho National Laboratory, with the first fueled reactor experiment starting as early as spring 2026.
*   Other recent DOE activities include American Nuclear Supply Chain Loans to rebuild the nuclear supply chain and accelerate the deployment of 10 new large-scale reactors, as well as negotiations to transform surplus plutonium into nuclear fuel.

**Artificial Intelligence (AI)**
*   President Trump's AI Strategy and Action Plan includes executive orders such as "Promoting Advanced AI Innovation and Security" (June 2, 2026) and "Ensuring a National Policy Framework for AI" (December 11, 2025).
*   The U.S. Department of State released its "Enterprise Artificial Intelligence Strategy FY 2024-2025: Empowering Diplomacy through Responsible AI," establishing guidance for the ethical design, development, acquisition, and application of AI. Secretary Blinken launched the Partnership for Global Inclusivity on AI (PGIAI) on September 23, 2024, with leading AI companies like Amazon, Anthropic, Apple, Google, IBM, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, and OpenAI, to leverage AI for sustainable development.
*   The DOE is partnering with private-sector developers to build cutting-edge AI data centers and energy-generation projects on DOE lands, and launched the Speed to Power Initiative to accelerate grid infrastructure development for AI.
*   The National Science Foundation (NSF) dedicated $140 million in May 2023 to launch seven new National AI Research Institutes to promote responsible innovation and bolster AI R&D infrastructure.

### Magnificent 7 Companies, Prominent Investors, or Industry Figures Investments

**Peter Thiel**
*   Thiel Macro, Peter Thiel's investment firm, re-entered the disclosed U.S. equity market in Q2 2026 with an equity portfolio exceeding $418 million across eight companies. Instead of focusing on semiconductor manufacturers, Thiel invested in electrical grid operators, nuclear developers (including X-Energy), tech infrastructure, and conventional energy, indicating a focus on the power infrastructure necessary for AI expansion.
*   Thiel Macro's largest purchase was 495,000 shares of Amazon (AMZN), representing approximately 28% of his portfolio, likely a bet on Amazon's AI infrastructure and cloud computing leadership.
*   Recent private investments by Peter Thiel through various rounds in 2026 include Etched (Series D, $700M, August 18, 2026), Panthalassa (Series B, $140M, May 4, 2026), and Objection AI (Seed, April 15, 2026). Thiel is also an early investor in OpenAI.

**Elon Musk (SpaceX, xAI)**
*   SpaceX became a publicly traded company on Nasdaq ($SPCX) on June 12, 2026, marking the largest IPO in history, raising $85 billion.
*   SpaceX acquired Elon Musk's AI company xAI in 2025 (now operating as SpaceXAI). xAI develops the Grok family of large language models and operates the social network X (formerly Twitter). This acquisition aims to build AI that "understands the true nature of the universe" and positions SpaceX as a meaningful player in AI infrastructure through space-based computing. SpaceX plans to launch a constellation of satellites to operate as orbital data centers powered by solar energy.
*   In May 2026, Elon Musk personally acquired mobile turbine manufacturer APR Energy for over $1 billion to power AI data centers.
*   SpaceX also acquired the AI coding platform Cursor for $60 billion on June 16, 2026.
*   SpaceX announced a joint venture with Tesla, Inc. in 2026 to build Terafab, a large plant for semiconductor device fabrication.

**Amazon**
*   Amazon and AT&T partnered in September 2026 to deliver satellite internet to business customers using Amazon's Leo low-Earth-orbit satellite division. Amazon Leo began enterprise previews in November 2025 and plans commercial service this year.
*   Amazon filed an application with the FCC in July 2026 to launch up to 5,105 additional satellites for direct-to-smartphone connectivity, with deployment starting in 2028. An existing agreement with Apple will power satellite features on supported iPhone and Apple Watch models.
*   Amazon is also expected to take control of Globalstar's satellites following an $11.57 billion deal announced in April 2026, anticipated to close in 2027.

**Google**
*   NextEra Energy agreed in October 2025 to restart the Duane Arnold nuclear power station, Iowa's only nuclear plant, primarily to provide power to Google as the tech giant seeks clean energy for its AI data centers. The DOE recently closed a $1.9 billion loan for this project.
